title: Fleischmann's 30-Minute Pizza Crust
reason: Complete source recipe; no equivalent indexed recipe, or a materially different ingredient/method variant.
body_html:
Ingredients

  • 1 3/4 to 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
  • 1 packet Fleischmann's Pizza Crust Yeast
  • 1 1/2 teaspoons sugar
  • 3/4 teaspoon salt
  • 2/3 cup very warm water (120-130 F)
  • 3 tablespoons oil
  • Pizza sauce, toppings, and cheese

Instructions

  1. Heat the oven to 425 F. Mix 1 cup flour with the undissolved yeast, sugar, and salt.
  2. Stir in water and oil for about 1 minute. Add enough remaining flour to make a soft, slightly sticky dough.
  3. Knead on a floured surface for about 4 minutes, adding flour as needed, until smooth and elastic.
  4. Pat into a greased pizza pan or roll into a 12-inch circle and transfer to a greased pan. Add sauce, toppings, and cheese.
  5. Bake on the bottom oven rack for 12-15 minutes, until the crust browns and cheese bubbles.

Source attribution: Fleischmann's package recipe, titled 30-Minute Pizza. Makes one regular 12-inch crust or two thin crusts. Directions adapted from the supplied clipping.

title: Grissini Breadsticks
reason: Complete source recipe; no equivalent indexed recipe, or a materially different ingredient/method variant.
body_html:
Ingredients

  • 1 cup warm water (105-115 F)
  • 2 1/4 teaspoons active dry yeast (1 package)
  • 1/4 cup olive oil
  • 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 cup semolina flour
  • 2 teaspoons honey
  • 2 teaspoons salt
  • Seasoning: 1 tablespoon each dried oregano, dried basil, dried parsley, red pepper flakes, and granulated garlic; 1 1/2 teaspoons dried rosemary; 1 teaspoon each fennel seeds and kosher salt

Instructions

  1. Dissolve active dry yeast in the warm water and wait 5-10 minutes for foam. Stir in oil and honey. For instant yeast, mix it with the flour instead.
  2. Combine both flours and salt, then add to the liquid. Knead 10 minutes until smooth; hand-kneaded dough may need 2 tablespoons extra flour. Rest 5 minutes.
  3. Stretch into a 14-by-4-inch rectangle. Brush with olive oil, cover the top and sides with plastic wrap, and proof at room temperature for 1 hour.
  4. Heat the oven to 450 F. Uncover and oil the dough again. Divide into quarters and keep unused portions covered.
  5. Pulse the seasoning ingredients in a small food processor. Press 2 teaspoons of seasoning onto each dough quarter, reaching the edges. Cut each quarter into 6 strips.
  6. Stretch each strip to 14-16 inches, twist, and arrange on parchment-lined baking sheets.
  7. Bake one sheet at a time for 10-12 minutes, turning the sticks after 6 minutes, until lightly browned.

Other toppings named in the source: coarse salt and pepper, sesame, Parmesan, poppy seeds, sun-dried tomato, or fennel and salt.

Ingredients

  • 3 cups flour
  • 2 teaspoons baking powder (3 teaspoons at high altitude)
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1 1/2 cups warm water or milk
  • 1 tablespoon oil
  • Vegetable oil for frying

Instructions

  1. Combine the ingredients, adding liquid gradually to form dough. Knead on a lightly floured surface until smooth without stickiness.
  2. Cover and rest 1 hour. Divide into small balls and flatten into circles 1/4-1/2 inch thick.
  3. Heat 1/2 inch vegetable oil in a skillet. Fry the circles until browned on both sides, then drain on paper towels.

Directions adapted from the supplied single-recipe sheet.

title: Swig Sugar Cookies
body_html:
Available ingredient facts

  • Cookies: 1 cup butter, softened
  • 3/4 cup avocado oil (cup unit recovered from original)
  • 1 1/4 cups granulated sugar
  • 3/4 cup powdered sugar
  • 1/2 teaspoon each baking soda, cream of tartar, and salt
  • 2 tablespoons sour cream
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 5 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
  • Granulated sugar for pressing
  • Frosting: 3/4 cup butter, softened
  • 2 tablespoons sour cream
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 6 cups powdered sugar
  • 1-2 tablespoons cream or milk

Instructions (concise adaptation)

  1. Heat oven to 350 F (325 F convection). Line baking sheets with parchment.
  2. Beat butter, oil, both sugars, baking soda, cream of tartar, and salt until creamy, 1-2 minutes. Beat in sour cream, eggs, and vanilla for another 1-2 minutes.
  3. Mix in flour just until combined. Roll approximately 3-tablespoon portions into balls, spacing them several inches apart.
  4. Dip the greased base of a flat-bottomed glass into granulated sugar and press each ball to 1/4-1/2 inch thick, dipping again between cookies.
  5. The supplied version specifies 10-12 minutes until just set, without browned edges. The current original instead specifies 7-9 minutes until edges are set. This page preserves the supplied version rather than silently replacing its timing.
  6. Cool briefly on the sheets, then completely on a rack. Beat frosting butter, sour cream and vanilla until smooth; mix in powdered sugar and cream or milk to a spreadable consistency. Frost cooled cookies; the supplied version says to serve chilled.

Yield: 30 cookies.

Original identified: Mel Gunnell, Mel's Kitchen Cafe, The Best Swig Sugar Cookies. The cookie/frosting cup quantities, yield, and distinctive preparation sequence match the supplied document. The original explicitly gives 3/4 cup oil; only that missing unit was recovered. The supplied avocado-oil substitution is retained. Current original weight conversions, oil options, and baking time differ and were not substituted. Directions are newly summarized, not copied.

  • 1 tablespoon sugar

  • 2 cups milk
  • 1/2 teaspoon vanilla
  • 2 eggs
  • 2 tablespoons butter, melted

title: Spiced Shredded Pork
reason: Complete source recipe; no equivalent indexed recipe, or a materially different ingredient/method variant.
body_html:
Ingredients

  • 1 pound pork tenderloin
  • 2 (14 1/2-ounce) cans low-sodium chicken stock (about 4 cups)
  • 2 small onions, finely chopped (about 1/2 cup)
  • 1/2 fresh jalapeno with seeds, finely chopped
  • 1/2 bunch cilantro (2 1/2-3 cups), plus garnish
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground cumin
  • 1 bay leaf
  • Coarse salt and freshly ground pepper
  • 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted
  • 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil

Instructions

  1. Preheat the broiler. Combine pork, stock, half the onion, jalapeno, cilantro, cumin, bay leaf, and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then simmer, stirring occasionally.
  2. The source specifies 10-15 minutes and 140 F before broiling. Transfer to a rimmed baking sheet and shred into 2-inch pieces.
  3. Add the remaining onion, butter, and oil, and season with salt and pepper. Broil 4-7 minutes until golden.

Adapted from the supplied sheet. Food safety: the source's 140 F interim temperature is not the final safe temperature. Whole-cut pork must reach 145 F and rest at least 3 minutes before serving.

title: Simone's Brazilian Black Beans

body_html:
Ingredients

  • 2 cups black beans
  • 6 cups water
  • 1 onion, diced
  • 6 garlic cloves, finely diced
  • 3 bay leaves
  • 2 sausage links (chorizo or another preferred sausage)
  • Kosher salt
  • 2 tablespoons oil for sauteing
  • Pepper to season

Instructions

  1. Soak the beans overnight, then rinse and remove small stones. Put in a pressure cooker with water 4 inches above the beans, as directed in the source. Cook 30 minutes, following the cooker's safety instructions.
  2. Saute the onion and garlic in 2 tablespoons oil. Add 4 large spoonfuls of cooked beans, mash with a fork, and season with salt and pepper.
  3. Return the skillet contents to the beans. Add sausage and cook another 15 minutes, checking doneness and water level and adding water if needed.
  4. Slice the cooked sausage and return it to the beans.

Source attribution: Simone's Brazilian Black Beans (For a pressure cooker). The ingredient list gives 6 cups water; the directions separately call for 4 inches above the beans. Both source statements are retained; no pressure setting is specified. Do not exceed your cooker's bean-fill limit.

title: Red Beans with Cheese

body_html:
Ingredients

  • 2 (19-ounce) cans kidney beans (about 4 cups), drained and rinsed
  • 2 (14 1/2-ounce) cans low-sodium chicken stock (about 4 cups)
  • 2 bay leaves
  • 1 medium onion, quartered
  • 1 fresh jalapeno with seeds, quartered
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
  • Coarse salt
  • 1/4 cup grated cotija cheese

Instructions

  1. Combine beans, stock, bay leaves, onion, jalapeno, cumin, and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then briskly simmer 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
  2. Strain and keep 1/2 cup cooking liquid. Discard the onion, jalapeno, and bay leaves.
  3. Return beans and reserved liquid to the pan with 2 tablespoons cheese. Mash about half the beans, leaving the rest whole.
  4. Serve warm with the remaining 2 tablespoons cheese.

Directions adapted from the supplied single-recipe sheet.
